entries.context: Topology · retrocompact open subset
entries.definition: Let X be a topological space. An open subset U⊆X is retrocompact in X if, for every quasi-compact open V⊆X, the intersection U∩V is quasi-compact. Equivalently, the inclusion U↪X is a quasi-compact map.

U∩V is quasi-compact relative to subspace topology for each quasi-compact open V.

entries.context: Algebra · multiplicity of polynomial root
entries.definition: Let F be a field, let f∈F[T] be a nonzero polynomial, and let α belong to a field extension E/F. The element α is a repeated (multiple) root of f if (T−α)² divides f in E[T]; equivalently, f(α)=f′(α)=0.

entries.term: Euclidean metric on the real line
entries.context: Real analysis · usual distance on R
entries.definition: The usual Euclidean metric on the real line ℝ is d:ℝ×ℝ→[0,∞), defined by d(a,b)=|a−b| for every a,b∈ℝ.

entries.context: Set theory · symmetry axiom for binary relation
entries.definition: A binary relation R⊆S×S on a set S is symmetric if, for every x,y∈S, xRy implies yRx.

entries.context: Elementary number theory: congruence of integers modulo a fixed positive integer
entries.definition:
For m∈ℤ with m>0 and a,b∈ℤ, define a≡b (mod m) if and only if there exists k∈ℤ such that a−b=km. The modulus m is fixed and strictly positive.

Equivalent formulation: Let m be a positive integer. For a,b∈ℤ write a≡b (mod m) precisely when the least nonnegative remainders of a and b upon division by m coincide.

entries.definition: For a unital ring R and an integer n≥1, the n×n identity matrix Iₙ has (Iₙ)ᵢⱼ=1_R when i=j and 0_R otherwise. It is the multiplicative identity of the matrix ring Mₙ(R).

entries.context: Order theory · upper-bounded subset of a poset
entries.definition: A subset A of a partially ordered set (P,≤) is bounded above in P if there exists u∈P such that a≤u for every a∈A. Such a u is called an upper bound of A. No least-upper-bound assumption is implied.

entries.context: Complex analysis · absolute value of a complex number
entries.definition: For a complex number z=a+bi with a,b∈ℝ, its modulus is |z|=√(a²+b²), the nonnegative Euclidean distance from z to the origin in the complex plane.

entries.context: Real analysis · punctured neighborhood of a point
entries.definition: For a∈ℝ and δ>0, the deleted (punctured) δ-neighborhood of a is {x∈ℝ:0<|x−a|<δ}. If considering a function with domain D, the relevant deleted neighborhood within its domain is its intersection with D.
